analysis.title: Back to the Monetary Future: Chartbook, In Gold We Trust Report 2026
key_insights: The authors argue gold is being remonetized through six vectors: central bank buying, reserve function and repatriation, private investor allocation, digitalization (Tether holding gold), gold-backed bonds as a credibility anchor, and revaluation of US gold reserves.

Gold closed at USD 4,067 on 10/28/2026, down 5.7% year to date and about 25% below the all-time high of USD 5,399 set on January 28, 2026. The authors say the pullback has not undone the rally of the last two years.

Gold's third great bull market has set 115 all-time highs so far, compared with 209 in the 1970s and 106 in the 2000s. Annual average prices have risen every year since 2016, which ties the longest streak since 1970.

Central banks bought an average of 245 tonnes per quarter after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine versus 118 tonnes before it. In Q1 2026 the top three sellers were Turkey (-79 tonnes), Russia (-22) and Azerbaijan (-22). ETF investors set the tempo of gold flows while central banks anchor demand.

Gold's share of global reserves is now about a quarter, up from 9% in 2015. Private investors hold only 2.7% of their assets in gold versus the 1980 peak of 8.25%. The authors say no investor group is close to its optimal gold allocation.

The proposed 'new 60/40' portfolio is 45% stocks, 15% bonds, 15% safe-haven gold, 10% performance gold, 10% commodities and 5% Bitcoin. The case rests on fiscal stress, expensive equities and an unreliable bond hedge. Privately held gold is only USD 8.6 trn against USD 312.0 trn of global financial assets, so a small shift would be large for gold.

Silver is down 24.3% year to date in USD and 53.7% below its January 28 high. The gold/silver ratio rose from 46 to 75 since January, and silver's one-year beta to gold rose to 1.9, the highest since 2021. The authors call this a correction in price, not in fundamentals, and note silver has been in deficit every year since 2019.

About 74% of silver comes as a by-product of copper, zinc, lead and gold mining, so silver supply does not respond to the silver price. The 1980 and 2011 highs are described as the key line in the sand for silver.

Gold miners are down 28% from the February peak but up 560% from the 2016 low. GDX is 27.5% below its high and GDXJ 33.2% below. Miners' leverage to the metals (rolling beta of GDX to gold) has fallen to the low end of its range.

GDX trailing earnings are up about fivefold since Q2/2023 while its P/E has been cut roughly in half. Margins are at multi-year highs and Q3 results will show whether margin expansion has peaked. The Active Aurum Signal has been defensive since March 2026, which the authors call a tactical pause, not a structural verdict.

The authors present a fiscal-stress case: US public debt has grown faster than GDP since 1960, deficits persist across major economies, and 10-year yields in France, Germany, Italy and the US are at their highest since 2002-2012 and breaking out. French 5-year CDS has overtaken Italy's.

US equities look expensive by the CAPE ratio (cheaper 98.6% of the time since 1900), and tech weight in the S&P 500 now exceeds the dot-com peak. The positive stock-bond correlation is easing, but the next equity sell-off will decide whether the bond hedge works.

Gold-implied monetary scenarios: the price needed to back 25% of the monetary base is USD 5,156, 40% is USD 8,457 and 100% is USD 21,143. The 2030 projection is USD 4,822 in the base case and USD 8,926 in the inflationary scenario, and the authors say gold currently trades between the two paths.

US gold reserves are carried at a book value of USD 11.0 bn (USD 42.22 per ounce) versus a market value of USD 1,086.8 bn, a revaluation gap of about USD 1.07 trn. Tether now holds enough gold to rank 30th among sovereign holders.

sector_views.rationale: The Active Aurum Signal has been defensive since March 2026 and miner leverage to gold is at the low end of its range. Earnings are up fivefold with the P/E cut in half, and Q3 margins are the test.
The new 60/40 portfolio cuts stocks to 45% from 60%. The authors cite a CAPE ratio that has been lower 98.6% of the time since 1900 and tech concentration above the dot-com peak.

Gold gets a 25% weight in the new 60/40 across safe-haven and performance sleeves, citing remonetization, central bank demand and fiscal stress. Silver's pullback is described as price-only, with a deficit every year since 2019.

earnings_insights: GDX last-twelve-months EPS rose about fivefold from Q2/2023 to Q2/2026 (chart labels 0.95 and 5.43), while the trailing P/E fell from 31.74 to 13.89. Q3 reporting is underway and the report says the bar is set high.
GDX margins (EBITDA, net and free cash flow) are at multi-year highs on a trailing basis. The report says Q3 will show whether margin expansion has peaked.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The authors' base-case path implies gold ends 2030 only about 19% above the 10/28/2026 price of USD 4,067.
The inflationary path is roughly 2.2 times the 10/28/2026 price. The authors say gold currently trades between the two paths.

crypto_views: Tether's gold holdings rank it 30th among national gold reserves (Q2/2026), ahead of Libya and just behind the Philippines on the chart. The report frames this as a digitalization vector for gold remonetization.
The new 60/40 portfolio includes a 5% Bitcoin allocation alongside 25% in gold.
The authors compare the market capitalizations of gold, silver, Bitcoin, NVIDIA and the S&P 500 against the gold and silver mining sub-industries.

trade_ideas.description: Shift to a 'new 60/40' portfolio: 45% stocks, 15% bonds, 15% safe-haven gold, 10% performance gold, 10% commodities, 5% Bitcoin, replacing the old 60% stocks and 40% bonds.
trade_ideas.rationale: Fiscal stress, expensive stocks and a shaky bond hedge add to the case, and privately held gold is only 2.7% of global financial assets.

risk_factors: ETF investors set the tempo of gold demand and can reverse flows quickly.
Central bank selling, as seen from Turkey (-79 tonnes), Russia and Azerbaijan in Q1 2026.
Miner margin expansion may have peaked, which Q3 results will show.
Silver's high beta to gold (1.9) works both ways, and silver is down 24.3% year to date.
The Active Aurum Signal has been defensive since March 2026.
A positive stock-bond correlation could leave bonds unable to hedge the next equity sell-off.
Past gold cycles ended with the Dow/Gold ratio well below its median of 7.24, and the report implies the current cycle has not yet reached that point.
charts_described: Global central bank gold purchases Q1/2010 to Q2/2026: average of 118 tonnes per quarter before the Russian invasion and 245 tonnes after.
Gold allocation by private investors 1970 to 2025: 8.25% at the 1980 high versus 2.70% in 2025.
Ranking of national gold reserves including Tether, Q2/2026: Tether ranks 30th, between the Philippines (31) and Libya (29).

US gold reserves as a percent of US public debt 1915 to 10/2026: a return to the 1980 ratio of 20.4% would imply a gold price of USD 31,312, 1917's 40.7% would imply USD 62,569 and 1940's 48.4% would imply USD 74,295, versus the current USD 4,067.
Gold from 01/2024 to 10/2026 with drawdown lines: USD 5,129 is -5% from the high, USD 4,859 is -10%, USD 4,589 is -15%, USD 4,319 is -20% and USD 4,049 is -25%.
Central bank, ETF and net gold flows Q1/2018 to Q2/2026: gold rose 57% in Q1/2018 to Q3/2020, 1% in Q2/2022 to Q1/2024 and 95% in Q3/2024 to Q4/2025.
Dow/Gold ratio 1900 to 10/2026: low 1.33, median 7.24, high 42.42.
Gold/silver ratio 2000 to 10/2026: 2000 average of 68.82, 1970 average of 60.29, 1900 average of 52.23.
Silver market balance including ETPs 2017 to 2025: surplus of 46.1 Moz in 2017 and 36.4 Moz in 2018, then deficits every year, ending with -318.4 Moz in 2025.
Gold miners bull and bear markets 1970 to 10/2026: bear markets of -68%, -83%, -67% and -83% and bull markets of 596%, 1,330%, 273%, 554% and 817%.
GDX trailing EPS and P/E Q2/2023 to Q2/2026: EPS from 0.95 to 5.43 and P/E from 31.74 to 13.89.

Market capitalization of the metals and their miners, 10/2026: precious metals and minerals mining sub-industry 84 USD bn, silver mining 90, gold mining 1,006 and Bitcoin 1,565, versus gold at 28,753 and the S&P 500 at 70,684 (chart order as extracted).
S&P 500 CAPE 1900 to 10/2026: median 16.53 and a level above 40 near the dot-com peak.
Composition of global total reserves 1970 to Q2/2026: gold now about a quarter of reserves, up from 9% in 2015.
vol_and_positioning: Private investors hold 2.7% of their assets in gold versus the 1980 peak of 8.25%.
No investor group (family offices, pensions, wealth managers and others) reaches the optimal gold allocation identified by the authors' sources.
Silver's rolling one-year beta to gold is 1.9, the highest since 2021, so it amplifies gold's moves in both directions.
The one-year beta of GDX to gold and of SIL to silver is at the low end of its range, so miners are not delivering their usual leverage to the metals.
The Incrementum Active Aurum Signal has been defensive since March 2026.
The 2-year rolling correlation of the S&P 500 to the US 10-year is easing from positive levels, and the next equity sell-off will decide whether bonds hedge again.
geopolitical: Russia's February 24, 2022 invasion of Ukraine and the freezing of Russian reserves, cited as the turning point for central bank gold buying.
The start of the Iran War on February 28, 2026, marked on the central bank and ETF flow chart.
Gold repatriation by national central banks from 2011 to 2026.
Central bank selling in Q1 2026 by Turkey, Russia and Azerbaijan.
French sovereign default protection costs breaking out and overtaking Italy's.
Tether entering the group of sovereign-scale gold holders.
cross_bank_references: Actual allocation data cited from JPMorgan 2026 FO Report, UBS GFO 2025 and Goldman Sachs FO 2025.
Optimal allocation sources cited include Morgan Stanley Wilson (Oct 2025) and the WGC Swiss Pension Study (Aug 2024).

tension_points.bull_case: Gold's third great bull market has set 115 all-time highs, central banks average 245 tonnes a quarter since 2022, and private investors hold only 2.7% in gold against 8.25% in 1980.
tension_points.bear_case: Gold is down about 25% from its January 28 high and 5.7% year to date, ETF investors set the tempo of flows, and Turkey, Russia and Azerbaijan sold gold in Q1 2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Past cycles ended with the Dow/Gold ratio well below its median of 7.24. The report does not give a price level that would end the current bull market.

tension_points.bull_case: GDX trailing earnings are up about fivefold, the P/E is cut roughly in half and margins are at multi-year highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Miners are down 28% from the February peak and their leverage to the metals has fallen to the low end of its range. The Active Aurum Signal has been defensive since March 2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 reporting showing that margin expansion has peaked.

tension_points.bull_case: The positive correlation between the S&P 500 and the US 10-year is easing, so bonds may regain their role as a hedge.
tension_points.bear_case: Bond yields in France, Germany, Italy and the US are at their highest since 2002-2012 and breaking out, and the report says the stock-bond correlation has been positive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next equity sell-off will decide whether bonds hedge again.

theme_stances.key_argument: Gold is regaining importance as a reserve asset that cannot be frozen, devalued, or denied access to at the push of a button.
Silver's price fell while fundamentals did not, with deficits every year since 2019 and by-product supply that does not follow the price.
theme_stances.evidence: A Correction in Price, Not in Fundamentals

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising debt, expensive stocks and a bond hedge that has been unreliable add to the case for holding gold, commodities and Bitcoin in the core portfolio.
theme_stances.evidence: Fiscal Stress, Pricey Stocks and a Shaky Bond Hedge
